title: Quick check: Code Splitting by Route

questions.prompt: Which statement best describes the purpose of “Code Splitting by Route”?
options: The concept removes the need to consider error states or accessibility.
The browser will infer all application behavior even if inputs and state are contradictory.
The concept allows application code to mutate React-managed DOM and state directly.
Lazy-loaded page components should be optimized only after measurement demonstrates a meaningful bottleneck.
questions.answer_key: Lazy-loaded page components should be optimized only after measurement demonstrates a meaningful bottleneck.
questions.explanation: The correct choice is grounded in Code Splitting by Route: Lazy-loaded page components should be optimized only after measurement demonstrates a meaningful bottleneck.

questions.prompt: Which practice is most reliable when applying Lazy-loaded page components?
options: Store duplicate copies of every value so each component can change it independently.
Optimize by adding every available Hook without measuring the result.
Profile a representative use case before adding memoization or restructuring code.
Skip validation because a successful render proves that the application is correct.
questions.answer_key: Profile a representative use case before adding memoization or restructuring code.
questions.explanation: The correct choice is grounded in Code Splitting by Route: Profile a representative use case before adding memoization or restructuring code.

questions.prompt: What should you verify before considering “Code Splitting by Route” complete?
options: Rely only on a screenshot of the happy path and never repeat the test.
Verify the documented result with a normal example and at least one boundary, loading, or failure case.
Check only whether the file exists; syntax and runtime behavior do not matter.
Assume a client-side check proves that a remote service accepted the change.
questions.answer_key: Verify the documented result with a normal example and at least one boundary, loading, or failure case.
questions.explanation: The correct choice is grounded in Code Splitting by Route: Verify the documented result with a normal example and at least one boundary, loading, or failure case.
